issues.description: Security question raised in PR description (revoke_error leakage) is unresolved
issues.detail: The author explicitly asks whether RevokeErr is safe to expose, noting it could contain sensitive info. The diff ships it anyway without a decision recorded. Knuth-style: state the invariant for what 'non-sensitive' means in the renamed leaseInfoForExport, or gate revoke_error behind a sudo/root check. Proved-correct vs tried-correct: neither here.

issues.description: Renamed function leaseInfoForExport lacks an explicit invariant of which fields are safe to export
issues.detail: The old name leaseTimesForExport was self-documenting; the new name promises 'non sensitive information' but defines it only by enumeration in the struct literal. A literate comment listing the redaction policy (what is included, what is deliberately omitted, why namespace pointer is safe to share) would make future additions safe-by-default rather than safe-by-accident.

issues.description: Shared namespace pointer copied into exported lease entry creates aliasing without stated contract
issues.detail: ret.namespace = le.namespace shares a pointer with the live lease entry. If any caller mutates the returned entry's namespace, it mutates the cached one. The export contract should state read-only or clone defensively. Same concern applies less acutely to Path (string, immutable) and RevokeErr.

issues.description: Test coverage for new fields is thin: only path is asserted, not namespace_path or revoke_error
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases adds a single assertion for path == 'secret/foo'. The two more interesting new outputs (namespace_path conditional on non-nil namespace with non-empty Path, and revoke_error conditional on non-empty string) have no test exercising the present and absent branches. Four small cases would lock the contract.

issues.description: Metric label 'expire.fetch-lease-times' was not updated when function was renamed
issues.detail: defer metrics.MeasureSince([]string{"expire", "fetch-lease-times"}, ...) retains the old name. Keeping the metric label stable is defensible (avoids breaking dashboards), but that decision should be a comment, not silence. Otherwise the next renamer will 'fix' it and break operators' alerts.

issues.description: Stale test function name TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable after API rename
issues.detail: The test still calls itself FetchLeaseTimes... but now exercises FetchLeaseInfo. Minor literate-programming hygiene: rename to match, or leave a one-line comment that the old name is intentionally preserved for git-blame continuity. Not a correctness issue.

review.summary: A clean, mostly mechanical rename (FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo, leaseTimesForExport -> leaseInfoForExport) plus three new exported fields on lease lookup. The algorithm and data structures are unchanged; no complexity concerns. UNDER-AUDITED on the security front: the author flags revoke_error as a possible leak vector and ships it without a stated policy. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on leaseInfoForExport: the redaction contract is implicit in a struct literal rather than written down, which will erode as fields are added. Tests assert only the easiest of the three new outputs. Verdict: RIGOROUS on the rename, UNDER-AUDITED on the new surface area.
